newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-SCALA LOOKS SET FOR DORTMUND JOB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCALA LOOKS SET FOR DORTMUND JOB.

text.p: European Cup holders Borussia Dortmund looked set on Friday to name Nevio Scala as their new coach after his current club Perugia agreed to release him from his contract.

Dortmund turned to the Italian, who guided Parma from the Italian second division to the European elite, after Ottmar Hitzfeld decided earlier this month to quit as coach and take over a new position as sports director at the club.

Germany's SID sports news agency said Perugia president Luciano Gaucci had told Scala, who had a contract tying him to the relegated Italian side until the year 2000, he was free to go after talks late on Thursday night.
"If he wants to reach an agreement with Dortmund, there are no problems on our side," it quoted Gaucci as saying.

Media reports said Scala was expected to fly into Germany on Friday night and sign a two-year contract on Saturday. Dortmund officials said they hoped to present their new coach at a news conference at the weekend or early next week.

Scala has made no secret of his interest in the Dortmund job, confirming he has held talks with the club and telling Germany's Kicker magazine this week: "It would be nice to take over the best team in Europe. I'm ready for Borussia."
The appointment would also meet with Hitzfeld's approval. "I wanted Scala to be my successor right from the beginning," he told Friday's edition of the Bild daily.
The Opera-loving coach -- who has a German wife -- would become the second Italian boss in the Bundesliga, joining Giovanni Trapattoni at champions Bayern Munich.
Scala, who coached Parma to the 1993 European Cup Winners' Cup and the 1995 UEFA Cup, has already set himself ambitious targets. "The championship would be a minimum aim," he said.
